behavioral_effects: 307 lines of never-executed generator-provided code deleted; the Python orphans list in orphans.json is now empty
compatibility_impact: None: all three modules had zero importers; versioning.py's URL scheme was never adopted (the /api/v1 prefix is hardcoded in route registration)
limitations: This does not add CSRF protection anywhere - it removes the illusion of it; the Bearer-token reliance is now recorded instead of implied
reason: Three generator-provided modules were never adopted: research.py is a re-export shim with zero importers, and the versioning and CSRF middleware were never registered in main.py; they are dead surface the orphans report carries and readers mistake for active defenses - in particular csrf.py suggests a cookie-CSRF layer that does not actually protect anything, while the app's real defense is Bearer-token auth
rollback: Revert the commit; the three modules return unchanged. They are also recoverable from the fastapi-fullstack template, their original provenance
security_impact: Deleting core/csrf.py removes no active defense: the middleware was never registered in main.py, so no request was ever CSRF-checked by it. Deliberately stated: this application relies on Bearer-token authentication in the Authorization header rather than cookie-based sessions, so cookie-CSRF middleware defends a surface the app does not expose. If cookie-session auth is ever introduced, CSRF defense must be re-evaluated then
summary: Delete three never-wired backend modules: agents/tools/research.py, api/versioning.py, core/csrf.py
